CALIFORNIA FRANCHISE INVESTMENT LAW AND FRANCHISE RELATIONS ACT — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme Franchising, Inc.

PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet, prepared by Pat Morgan, states what California law provides about two related but distinct statutory schemes governing franchises in California: the pre-sale disclosure and registration requirements of the Franchise Investment Law (Cal. Corp. Code §§ 31000 et seq.), which apply to the offer or sale of a franchise, and the termination and non-renewal protections of the California Franchise Relations Act (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 20000-20043), which apply to an existing franchise relationship. Where a specific business name is named below, that is Acme Franchising, Inc.; this sheet can also be read on its own, without it filled in, as a general reference to what these statutes say. This sheet states the law; it does not evaluate whether any particular arrangement is a "franchise," whether any particular offer or sale complied with the Franchise Investment Law, or whether any particular termination or non-renewal was lawful, and it is not a substitute for individualized legal advice.

DEFINITION OF A "FRANCHISE" UNDER CALIFORNIA LAW
California law defines "franchise" in materially the same three-part terms in two separately codified places. Under the Franchise Investment Law, a "franchise" is a contract or agreement, express or implied, oral or written, between two or more persons, by which a franchisee is granted the right to engage in the business of offering, selling, or distributing goods or services under a marketing plan or system prescribed in substantial part by a franchisor; the franchisee's business under that plan or system is substantially associated with the franchisor's trademark, service mark, trade name, or other commercial symbol; and the franchisee is required to pay, directly or indirectly, a franchise fee. The California Franchise Relations Act defines "franchise," for its own separate purposes, in the same three-part terms.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Franchise” means a contract or agreement, either expressed or implied, whether oral or written, between two or more persons by which: (1) A franchisee is granted the right to engage in the business of offering, selling or distributing goods or services under a marketing plan or system prescribed in substantial part by a franchisor; and (2) The operation of the franchisee’s business pursuant to such plan or system is substantially associated with the franchisor’s trademark, service mark, trade name, logotype, advertising or other commercial symbol designating the franchisor or its affiliate; and (3) The franchisee is required to pay, directly or indirectly, a franchise fee."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 31005(a), Franchise Investment Law, definition of "franchise" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=31005.)
  "“franchise” means a contract or agreement, either expressed or implied, whether oral or written, between two or more persons by which: (a) A franchisee is granted the right to engage in the business of offering, selling or distributing goods or services under a marketing plan or system prescribed in substantial part by a franchisor; and (b) The operation of the franchisee’s business pursuant to that plan or system is substantially associated with the franchisor’s trademark, service mark, trade name, logotype, advertising, or other commercial symbol designating the franchisor or its affiliate; and (c) The franchisee is required to pay, directly or indirectly, a franchise fee."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20001(a)-(c), California Franchise Relations Act, definition of "franchise" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=20001.)
  Known gap: Cal. Corp. Code § 31005(a) and Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20001(a)-(c) are two independently numbered sections in two different codes, not subdivisions of the same section — the two citations below are independent of one another, though the operative language is nearly identical. This clause does not restate Corp. Code § 31005(b), which extends "franchise" to certain petroleum-marketing arrangements, or § 31005(c), which excludes certain nonprofit cooperative wholesaling organizations; it does not restate Bus. & Prof. Code § 20001(d), which excludes Petroleum Marketing Practices Act franchises, certain incidental retail lease departments and concessions (under 10% of an establishment's sales), and the same category of nonprofit cooperatives. It also does not address the separate statutory extensions of "franchise" to "area franchise" and "subfranchise" arrangements (Corp. Code § 31010; Bus. & Prof. Code § 20006), or the "franchise fee" definition and its own carve-outs (Corp. Code § 31011; Bus. & Prof. Code § 20007). This clause does not evaluate whether any particular business arrangement meets this definition.

PRE-SALE REGISTRATION REQUIREMENT
It is unlawful for any person to offer or sell a franchise in California unless the offer of the franchise has been registered with the Commissioner of Financial Protection and Innovation under the Franchise Investment Law, or is exempted under the law's own exemption provisions.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "On and after April 15, 1971, it shall be unlawful for any person to offer or sell any franchise in this state unless the offer of the franchise has been registered under this part or exempted under Chapter 1 (commencing with Section 31100) of this part."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 31110, Franchise Investment Law, registration requirement for the offer or sale of a franchise (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=31110.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only Corp. Code § 31110, the operative registration requirement; it does not enumerate the exemptions found in Chapter 1 (Corp. Code §§ 31100-31109.1), which that section itself cross-references, and it does not restate the registration application, escrow, or stop-order process (Corp. Code §§ 31111-31118) or the one-year duration and renewal of an effective registration (Corp. Code §§ 31120-31121). It does not evaluate whether any particular offering is registered, exempt, or otherwise compliant.

THE 14-DAY FRANCHISE DISCLOSURE DOCUMENT DELIVERY REQUIREMENT
Separately from the registration requirement, where a franchise is subject to registration, California law makes it unlawful to sell that franchise without first giving the prospective franchisee a copy of the franchise disclosure document, together with copies of all proposed agreements relating to the sale, at least 14 days before whichever comes first: the prospective franchisee's execution of any binding franchise or other agreement, or the franchisor's receipt of any consideration.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "It is unlawful to sell any franchise in this state that is subject to registration under this law without first providing to the prospective franchisee, at least 14 days prior to the execution by the prospective franchisee of any binding franchise or other agreement, or at least 14 days prior to the receipt of any consideration, whichever occurs first, a copy of the franchise disclosure document, together with a copy of all proposed agreements relating to the sale of the franchise."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 31119(a), Franchise Investment Law, the 14-day pre-sale disclosure document requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=31119.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only Corp. Code § 31119(a); it does not restate § 31119(b), which addresses electronic delivery of the disclosure document, or the separate requirements governing the disclosure document's required contents (Corp. Code § 31114) and the registration's effective date (Corp. Code § 31116). It does not evaluate whether any particular disclosure document was timely delivered or complete.

GOOD CAUSE REQUIREMENT AND THE NOTICE-AND-CURE PERIOD FOR TERMINATION
Except as otherwise provided by the California Franchise Relations Act, a franchisor may not terminate a franchise before the end of its stated term except for good cause. Except for the circumstances the Act treats separately as warranting immediate termination, "good cause" is limited to the franchisee's failure to substantially comply with the lawful requirements the franchise agreement imposes on the franchisee — and only after the franchisor has given the franchisee at least 60 days' advance notice of the termination and a reasonable cure opportunity of no less than 60 days from the date of that notice. The cure period the franchisor must allow is not required to exceed 75 days, unless the franchisor and franchisee separately agree to extend it.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Except as otherwise provided by this chapter, no franchisor may terminate a franchise prior to the expiration of its term, except for good cause. Except as provided in Section 20021, good cause shall be limited to the failure of the franchisee to substantially comply with the lawful requirements imposed upon the franchisee by the franchise agreement after being given notice at least 60 days in advance of the termination and a reasonable opportunity, which in no event shall be less than 60 days from the date of the notice of noncompliance, to cure the failure. The period to exercise the right to cure shall not exceed 75 days unless there is a separate agreement between the franchisor and franchisee to extend the time."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20020, California Franchise Relations Act, good cause requirement and notice-and-cure period for termination (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=20020.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20020 in full; it is a single section, not a composite of independent sections. It does not restate the separate list, in Bus. & Prof. Code § 20021, of circumstances (such as bankruptcy, abandonment of the business, felony conviction, or repeated noncompliance) under which the Act itself deems immediate termination without a cure opportunity reasonable — those circumstances are an exception to, not a restatement of, the general rule quoted here. It also does not restate the franchisor's post-termination repurchase obligations under Bus. & Prof. Code § 20022. It does not evaluate whether good cause existed, or whether required notice was given, in any particular termination.

THE 180-DAY NOTICE REQUIREMENT FOR NON-RENEWAL
As a general rule, a franchisor may not fail to renew a franchise unless the franchisor gives the franchisee at least 180 days' prior written notice of its intention not to renew. California's Franchise Relations Act then attaches that general 180-day notice rule to a further set of conditions that vary depending on the circumstances of the non-renewal.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "No franchisor may fail to renew a franchise unless such franchisor provides the franchisee at least 180 days prior written notice of its intention not to renew;"
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20025, California Franchise Relations Act, the 180-day prior written notice requirement for non-renewal (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=20025.)
  Known gap: The quoted text is the opening clause of Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20025, which continues into six lettered conditions, (a) through (f) — covering a franchisee's opportunity to sell the business, non-competition covenants, non-renewals that would otherwise qualify as terminations for good cause under §§ 20020-20021, mutual agreement, franchisor withdrawal from a market, and failure to agree on renewal terms — that this clause does not restate. It also does not address § 20026, which permits a franchisor to offer a limited term extension to satisfy the 180-day notice period. This clause does not evaluate whether required notice was given, or which of § 20025's conditions applied, in any particular non-renewal.

FORM AND CONTENT OF A NOTICE OF TERMINATION OR NON-RENEWAL
Every notice of termination or non-renewal that the California Franchise Relations Act requires must be in writing; must be sent by registered mail, certified mail, other receipted mail, or telegram, or personally delivered, to the franchisee; and must state the franchisor's intent to terminate or not renew the franchise, together with the reasons for it and the effective date of the termination, non-renewal, or expiration.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "All notices of termination or nonrenewal required by this chapter: (a) Shall be in writing; (b) Shall be posted by registered, certified or other receipted mail, delivered by telegram or personally delivered to the franchisee; and (c) Shall contain a statement of intent to terminate or not renew the franchise: (1) Together with the reasons therefor, and (2) The effective date of such termination or nonrenewal or expiration."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20030, California Franchise Relations Act, form and content requirements for notices of termination or non-renewal (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=20030.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 20030 in full; it is a single section. The statute does not itself specify how compliance with its delivery methods is proven, and this clause does not address that. It does not evaluate whether any particular notice satisfied these form and content requirements.

SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATION
I, Pat Morgan, certify that I prepared this information sheet as a summary of the Franchise Investment Law (Cal. Corp. Code §§ 31000 et seq.) and the California Franchise Relations Act (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 20000-20043), for informational reference only. This information sheet does not evaluate whether Acme Franchising, Inc. is a party to a "franchise" as these statutes define it, whether any offer, sale, termination, or non-renewal involving Acme Franchising, Inc. complied with these statutes, and is not a substitute for consulting a person licensed to practice law in the relevant jurisdiction.

Business name under consideration, if applicable: Acme Franchising, Inc.

Executed on September 4, 2026 at Sacramento, California.

Signature of Pat Morgan: ☐ _________________________
